text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
SABAH
- Large funeral in Ankara for 11 military staff killed in a helicopter crash in northern Iraq.
- Turkish parliament passes law to close down casinos. The new law will be effective six months after it is published in the official gazette.
MILLIYET
- Army puts embargo on military units trading with shops linked to Islamist organisations.
- Joint protest by workers and employees against the Islamist-led coalition is to be held on Friday.
HURRIYET
- Conservative coalition partner Tansu Ciller says she will pull out of the government if she is not handed the premiership in a fortnight.
YENI YUZYIL
- Television correspondent who was shot and injured this week says organised crime bosses are behind the attack.
- Three leading conservatives hold anti-government talks.
RADIKAL
- President Suleyman Demirel wants military to stay away from politics.
DUNYA
- The Council of State takes decision to freeze Islamist-led government plan to gather all state accounts into one cash pool.
ZAMAN
- Conservative main opposition deputy Ismail Durak Unlu joined the far-righ Grand Unity Party after he resigned from his party.
CUMHURIYET

- The coalition partners cannot reach agreement on the handling of the premiership to Ciller as Islamist put a condition asking for a guarantee that their party would not be shut down by constitutional court.
